solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put out about underwear once split from below?

indicators.note: a word put out of joint is disordered, so its letters are rearranged
about means going round, so the rearranged letters wrap around the next item

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
bras are items of women's underwear

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that their underwear has ripped at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: UPBRAST is Spenser's past form of upburst; 'once' flags the archaic word, and the question mark admits the definition is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: To upburst is to burst upwards, so something upbrast has split open from beneath.

clue.text: Zealot does without brown bread, fried

indicators.note: doing without something means losing it, so a word is removed from the longer one

blocks.note: a Puritan is a strict religious zealot
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A fanatic refuses brown bread and fried food.
explanation.walkthrough: PURITAN without TAN leaves PURI.
explanation.definitionFit: Puri is an Indian unleavened bread deep-fried until it puffs up.

clue.text: Wild bush, old, live, about erect

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: to be is to live or exist
to rear something is to raise it upright

explanation.surface: A description of an ancient wild shrub growing upright.
explanation.walkthrough: B(REAR)E: the two letters for 'live' go round the word for 'erect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Breare is an obsolete Spenserian spelling of briar, a thorny wild shrub.

clue.text: Rodent I found under a bed

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so this letter follows the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
a couch is a bed or sofa to lie on
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has discovered a rodent hiding under the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The acouchi is a small South American rodent related to the agouti.

clue.text: Salt nets form of red tiddler

indicators.note: a form of a word is a reshaping of it, so its letters are rearranged
to net something is to catch it inside, so one part is enclosed by another

blocks.note: sal is the Latin and chemists' word for salt
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A salty old sailor catches a little red fish in his nets.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardel is a small fish like a sardine, so a tiddler in the sense of a little fish.

clue.text: Radio lever maybe, one clot adjusted, torn off within (11, two words)

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so these letters are rearranged
off means awry or wrong, so this word's letters are also jumbled
within places the second jumble inside the first

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A clumsy person has fiddled with a radio and ripped a lever off.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: ONE CLOT jumbled forms the outside, and TORN jumbled sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone control is a knob or slider on a radio that adjusts bass and treble, so an example of a lever.

clue.text: Wander about for Scotch, last to leave pub

indicators.note: the final letter departs, so the word is cut short at its end

blocks.note: a tavern is an inn or pub

explanation.surface: A drinker staggers from the pub after the last customer leaves, after some Scotch whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky in the pub, but here it means Scots: TAVER is a Scots dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, to taver (or taiver) is to wander aimlessly or ramble.

clue.text: Fix with lashes following criminal charge

blocks.note: f is the standard abbreviation for following
a rap is slang for a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: A prisoner is flogged after being convicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lashes' suggests whipping, but here it means ropes binding things tight.
explanation.definitionFit: In nautical use, to frap is to bind tightly with ropes or lashings.

clue.text: Remnant remaining when US leaves disturbance

indicators.note: these two letters depart from the word, so they are removed

blocks.note: a rumpus is a noisy commotion
taken as written

explanation.surface: What is left after the Americans pull out of a troubled region.
explanation.definitionFit: A rump is the small remaining part of something, like a rump parliament left after a purge.

clue.text: Register concerning deferral of payment

blocks.note: a roll is an official register of names
over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money

explanation.surface: Recording something in a register about putting off a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollover is the extension of a loan or debt, deferring repayment to a later date.

clue.text: Philanthrope keeps this anteater in hut

indicators.note: the longer word keeps only what lies between the letters of the other, which are thrown away

blocks.note: a humanist is concerned with human welfare, like a philanthropist
taken as written; these are the letters wrapped around the answer

explanation.surface: A kindly person keeps a pet anteater in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual construction: the definition sits inside the wordplay, and 'keeps' means the philanthrope's word contains the answer within the letters of 'hut'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manis is the genus name of the pangolin, the scaly anteater.

clue.text: Rarely favoured Communist dividing fortune before court

indicators.note: dividing means splitting another word, so this part is placed inside it
before means placed in front of what follows

blocks.note: a pile is a large fortune, as in making one's pile
red is the usual word for a Communist
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A Communist who seldom received favour splits a fortune before going to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' marks a rare word rather than meaning seldom.
explanation.definitionFit: Predilect is a rare adjective meaning chosen or preferred, akin to predilection.

clue.text: Treat sick pig, we hear? Strong medicine!

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the words are said aloud to give the answer

blocks.note: to cure an ailing female pig, a sow

explanation.surface: A vet treats an ill pig with powerful medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Curaçao is pronounced 'cure-a-sow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Curaçao is an orange-flavoured liqueur, humorously described as strong medicine.

clue.text: Carriage, one strong wind overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a means one
the bora is a cold strong wind on the Adriatic coast

explanation.surface: A gust of wind tips over a carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroba (or araba) is a heavy covered carriage used in Turkey and the Middle East.

clue.text: Old-time magistrate punished toper introducing rule

indicators.note: something punished is knocked about, so its letters are rearranged
introducing means bringing something in, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
R is the abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: A Roman judge sentences a drunkard under a new law.
explanation.walkthrough: A toper is a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretor is an old spelling of praetor, a Roman magistrate ranking below consul.

clue.text: Large bowl to spoil pet Spooner-wise? (9, two words)

indicators.note: in the manner of Spooner, the initial sounds of the two words are swapped

blocks.note: to cosset is to spoil or pamper, and a pup is a young pet dog

explanation.walkthrough: Swap the C and P sounds of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A posset cup is a large two-handled bowl for serving posset, a hot drink of curdled milk and wine.

clue.text: Dietary necessity, volume taken before a course

indicators.note: taken before means placed ahead, so these parts come first in sequence

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for volume
taken as written
a line is a course of action or direction

explanation.surface: A nutrition tip: take a large quantity before starting a course of treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Valine is an essential amino acid, one the body must obtain from food.

clue.text: Procession showing a barrel’s rolling out within

indicators.note: rolling means tumbling about, so these letters are rearranged
within places the jumbled letters inside the other words

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, as anagram fodder
a cade is a barrel or cask

explanation.surface: A parade where a barrel rolls out of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocade is a motorcade, a procession of cars.

clue.text: Damn Highlander plotted cunningly?

blocks.note: dee is a mild euphemism for damn
plaid can mean a person wearing one, a Highlander in tartan

explanation.surface: A Scottish Highlander curses a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-laid describes a scheme planned in secret with great care and cunning.

clue.text: Dead-head around entry to cottage, neat

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its opening letter
around means surrounding, so the first part goes round the selected letter

blocks.note: in metal casting, a sprue or dead-head is the waste metal left in the pouring channel
the first letter of cottage

explanation.surface: A gardener deadheads flowers around a cottage doorway, making things tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead-head' suggests snipping off spent flowers, but it is the founder's term for the waste plug of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and trim in appearance.

clue.text: Vocalize from bottom, cutting up

indicators.note: cutting means removing, so a two-letter word is taken out

blocks.note: croupon is an old word for the buttocks or rump
taken as written

explanation.surface: Singing from deep down, then cutting the volume.
explanation.walkthrough: CROUPON with UP removed leaves CROON.
explanation.definitionFit: To croon is to sing or hum softly, giving voice to a tune.

clue.text: This syndrome afflicts musicians? It’s universal in love poetry

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so this letter sits within another word

blocks.note: love is zero, the letter O, in tennis scoring
verse is poetry
U is the film-classification letter for universal

explanation.surface: A question about an ailment of performers, and a remark that it is common in romantic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside VERSE, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Overuse syndrome is a repetitive strain condition common in instrumentalists, from too much practice.

clue.text: Once ejected, so plenty reduced regularly

indicators.note: cut down at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Someone was thrown out once, so there are lots fewer people.
explanation.definitionFit: Spet is an obsolete past form of spit, so it means spat out or expelled from the mouth.

clue.text: American bluish cloth – it’s uniquely excellent

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
perse is an old grey-blue cloth or colour

explanation.surface: Praise for a blue American fabric as one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A-per-se literally means the letter A by itself, hence the first or best of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: An a-per-se is a person or thing of matchless excellence, a paragon.

clue.text: Old instrument I found in small book?

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the letter is placed within

blocks.note: vol is the short form of volume, a book
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has discovered an antique instrument illustrated in a little book.
explanation.definitionFit: The viol is a bowed string instrument of the Renaissance and Baroque, ancestor-cousin of the violin family.

clue.text: Train bursting with start of year? It’s likely to be full early on

definitions.text: It’s likely to be full early on

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
bursting means breaking apart, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the first letter of year

explanation.walkthrough: The second sentence is a cryptic definition: the office tray holding new papers is fullest at the start of the working day.

clue.text: Theatrical entertainment? Take a tipple before one

blocks.note: a dram is a small drink of spirits
a means one

clue.text: Without pressure coping reformed keystone

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped
reformed means made again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
taken as written, as anagram fodder

clue.text: Gadget? Force opening for one

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: gism is a variant of jism, meaning force or energy
the first letter of one

explanation.definitionFit: A gismo (or gizmo) is a gadget, a clever little device.

clue.text: Carp, English, no good in water

blocks.note: pee is informal for urine, passing water

ng is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A fish from England turns out to be no good in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish, but it is a verb meaning complain; PEENGE is Scots.

clue.text: Small distorted crystal struck in a jiffy

hit is struck

clue.text: Passed quickly over cache? Sounds like it

blocks.note: ca' is Scots for drive, as in driving cattle
taken as written, as anagram fodder

clue.text: US crawler chewed rag, in the groove (6, two words)

clue.text: Vault, as ours, say, when vandalized

clue.text: Wary regarding most people turning weird inside (7, two words)
